title: Securing Semiconductor Supply Chains Act of 2025
official_title: To require SelectUSA to coordinate with State-level economic development organizations to increase foreign direct investment in semiconductor-related manufacturing and production.
summary: The Securing Semiconductor Supply Chains Act directs SelectUSA — Commerce's investment promotion program — to consult with state economic development agencies about how to attract more foreign direct investment in U.S. semiconductor manufacturing. SelectUSA must report back to Congress within two years. No new funds are authorized.
brief: Directs SelectUSA to gather state agency input on attracting foreign investment in semiconductor manufacturing and report findings and strategies to Congress within two years.

top_lines.headline: State Input on Semiconductor Investment
subs: SelectUSA must solicit comments from state economic development organizations within 180 days on federal efforts to attract foreign direct investment in semiconductor fabrication, advanced packaging, and materials and equipment manufacturing

Comments must cover barriers to investment, public opportunities, and resource gaps; also recommendations on how SelectUSA can partner with states and protect U.S. efforts from benefiting foreign adversaries

top_lines.headline: Congressional Report Within Two Years
subs: SelectUSA must submit a report to Congress within 2 years covering: review of state comments, description of ongoing SelectUSA activities, and strategies for increasing semiconductor foreign direct investment
No additional funds are authorized for carrying out the Act

likelihoodReason: The bill passed the House in April 2025 with bipartisan support and was received in the Senate. Semiconductor supply chain security has broad bipartisan appeal. However, the bill is a study and coordination measure with no new funding, which reduces urgency. The 60-vote Senate threshold and low cosponsor count (2) suggest limited political organizing behind this bill.

items.main: Names the Act the “Securing Semiconductor Supply Chains Act of 2025”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

items.main: Defines “SelectUSA” as the SelectUSA program of the Department of Commerce established by Executive Order No. 13577 (76 Fed. Reg. 35715).

States congressional findings that semiconductors underpin the economy and national security, that pandemic-era shortages threatened recovery, and that SelectUSA can leverage foreign direct investment to secure vulnerable supply-chain segments.
items.detail: Findings section — context only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 4 — Coordination With State-Level Economic Development Organizations

items.main: Requires the Executive Director of SelectUSA, within 180 days of enactment, to solicit comments from state-level economic development organizations on supporting foreign direct investment in semiconductor-related production, barriers, public opportunities, and resource gaps.
items.detail: Organizations must also recommend how SelectUSA can increase investment alone or in partnership, and how to work with allies/partners so foreign adversaries (as defined in section 8(c)(2) of the Secure and Trusted Communications Networks Act of 2019, 47 U.S.C. 1607(c)(2)) do not benefit.

sections.label: Section 5 — Report on Increasing Foreign Direct Investment in Semiconductor-Related Manufacturing and Production

items.main: Requires SelectUSA, within 2 years of enactment and coordinating with the Federal Interagency Investment Working Group, to report to the Senate Commerce and House Energy and Commerce Committees on the comments received, current activities, and strategies to increase investment.
items.detail: The strategy assessment includes working with other federal agencies and with state-level organizations to implement their recommendations.

items.main: Provides that no additional funds are authorized to be appropriated to carry out the Act.

gaps: The bill requires SelectUSA to solicit state comments and report to Congress but does not require SelectUSA to implement any of the recommendations it receives or take any specific actions to increase semiconductor investment.

The bill restricts the scope to foreign direct investment but does not address domestic investment barriers in semiconductor manufacturing, which industry groups have identified as a parallel supply chain security concern.

added: Requirement for SelectUSA to solicit state economic development organization comments on semiconductor investment within 180 days
Congressional report due within 2 years on semiconductor investment strategies and state recommendations
